ShortDescription.Value: Play however your brain wants. The mod remembers the rest.

Publish.LongDescription:
# ADHD Gone Wild — seems about right.
Ever started fixing a roundabout… and ended up with three half-built metro lines, half a park, the beginning of a harbor, and no memory of the original problem?
Ever opened one panel… and suddenly the whole screen was yelling at you?
Ever played for “five more minutes”… and somehow it’s tomorrow?
No productivity hacks. No focus police. No forcing your brain into a checklist.
ADHD Gone Wild clears the noise, remembers the loose ends, and lets your brain wander wherever it wants.
## What it does
**Park an idea.** You are drawing a highway and suddenly think of a metro station. Press Ctrl+I, click that spot, and the thought is saved there with a ring you can see from the air. One keypress, one click. Then it offers - never demands - to say a little more:
> **Saved. Anything to add?** - Idea / Build something / Decoration / Transport / Fix or change
Click the ring any time to open what you left there, retitle it, or forget it. Nothing ever asks you to finish it, and nothing anywhere counts what you did not.
**Forty warnings become one line.** When a district loses power, the game puts the same icon over every building it touches. This gathers them into one row per problem, worst first, with a count:
> **Part of the city is without electricity** - 23 buildings
Click the row and the camera flies to them one at a time. Mute a kind of warning you have decided not to care about, and unmute it whenever you change your mind.
**Keep a way back.** Before you bulldoze half the centre, one click saves a checkpoint. It is a real save, kept apart from your own so it never clutters your list - and the panel keeps reminding you it is there, because a save you have forgotten gives you no courage:
> **You can come back to this** - 20 minutes ago - [Go back] [Keep what I did]
**Pick up where you left off.** Return to a city after a few days and a card names it, takes the camera back to where you were standing, and says what you parked there:
> **Welcome back to Pittston** - You were around here - 2 saved ideas here
**Turn the noise down.** The game's warning icons pulse to pull your eye; this holds them still without hiding anything - same place, same size, same meaning, just no movement. And a small button folds the entire build toolbar away, leaving only the bar with the clock, the population and the money. One click brings it all back.
**Reminds you to drink water - while you are hyperfocusing.** Hyperfocus does not take away your discipline. It takes away your sense of time passing. So every couple of hours a small card hands that back, with a short word about your body, and then gets out of the way:
> **23:40** - You have been here for 2 hours - *Water. Go on, I'll watch the city.*
That second line rotates: water, food, standing up, your eyes, your shoulders. After midnight it stops talking about posture and says *"Go to bed. That road will still be there tomorrow."* It never suggests stopping - reading it and carrying on building is a perfectly good outcome. You can switch the line off and keep the clock alone.
Everything can be switched off on its own. Nothing is written into your save games. English, French and Italian.
## Early days
This is a first release and the mod is nowhere near finished. Plenty is still planned, some of what is here will change, and a few things are certainly rough.
**Please leave a comment.** What helps, what gets in the way, what you wish it did. And if you have ADHD, how any of this actually lands for you - that is worth more to me than a bug report, because it is the part I cannot work out on my own.
## Thanks
To my girlfriend, and to her ADHD. Between them they shaped this mod far more than I did.
Publish.ChangeLog:
First release.
- Park an idea anywhere on the map and come back to it later, with a marker you can see. - Smart alerts: one row per kind of problem instead of one icon per building, with mute and unmute. - Creative safety net: a one-click checkpoint, and a one-click way back from it. - Welcome back: where you were, and what you left there. - Calm UI: notification icons held still, and a build toolbar that folds away. - Hyperfocus reminders: the wall clock and how long you have been playing. - Colour-blind friendly palette, and every feature switchable on its own. - English, French and Italian.
